audit.why: EVEN / 6/10 fits 49.54%. Shape is right: Gnar owns level 1, Sett owns 3 through 5 and the first item, and the late game levels out because Gnar becomes the teamfight engine rather than a duellist.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicted its own prose in four rows. mid says 'Levels 4-5 are the danger zone and they belong to Sett' while win[3] read Gnar; whys[2] says Sett's E flips level 3 while win[2] read Skill; whys[5] says his grit shield and first item out-sustain your poke while win[5] read Gnar; whys[6] says 'it levels out' while win[6] read Gnar. whys[0] says Mini wins the first trade while win[0] read Skill.
audit.why: Every one of those rows disagrees with the packet chart too (Gnar / Skill / Sett / Sett / Skill / Sett / Skill). Flipped as one atomic group across both layers, with the phases whys rewritten so the reasoning matches the new owner.
audit.corrected: win[0]=Gnar, win[2]=Sett, win[3]=Sett, win[5]=Sett, win[6]=Skill and the matching phases[N].side, with phases[2], [3], [5] and [6] whys restated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were never stated. (a) Facebreaker (E) stuns only when enemies are on opposite sides of Sett; with everything on one side it is a slow — the page calls it a 'grab-stun' unconditionally. (b) Haymaker (W) deals true damage in the centre and physical on the sides, so positioning off his midline is worth more than any armour, which is also the flagged resistances-invalidated gap.
audit.why: Both change what you actually do. Standing wave-side of Sett downgrades his only hard CC to a slow, and drifting off the centre of Haymaker turns unmitigable true damage into damage your armour reduces. 'Kite it' does not tell you either.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker (E, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) needs enemies on both sides to stun — keep the minion wave on your side of him. Haymaker (W, 18s at rank 1) is true damage only in its centre; the sides are physical. The Show Stopper is 120s at rank 1. Gnar's Hop is 22s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early, mid and late blocks are written in the first person ('are mine', 'I get a Mega Wallop', 'I die'), not the user's second-person voice.
audit.why: Every other field on the page addresses the reader directly; these three read like a diary entry.
audit.corrected: early and mid rewritten in second person at the same length. late left alone this pass — the fix there is voice-only and I would rather not spend band on a field with no factual error.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are mine — Mini's ranged autos plus a single Boomerang chip Sett before he has built any grit to make his W smash hurt, and the third-hit Hyper proc lets me land a chunky free trade and shove. Do NOT throw a Boomerang and then walk in to catch it inside his E range; the grab-stun plus a W loaded with the damage he just soaked erases the whole trade and then some. At 3 he flips it: his E comes online and he just walks me down if I am stuck in Mini, so kite the grab, last-hit at max range, and only commit once Rage is building.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are yours — Mini's ranged autos plus a single Boomerang chip Sett before he has stored grit to make Haymaker hurt, and the Hyper third-hit proc buys a chunky free trade and a shove. Never throw the Boomerang and then walk in to catch it inside Facebreaker range — the pull plus a loaded W erases the trade. At 3 his E arrives on 16 seconds, but read it properly: it stuns only when enemies sit on both sides of him, so keep the minion wave on your side and it is just a slow. Last-hit at max range and commit once Rage is building.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the danger zone and they belong to Sett. If my Rage lines up I get a Mega Wallop stun or wall-combo and I win the all-in outright — but if I am stuck in Mini with Rage on cooldown when he lands E, his W smash and Pit Grit punches shred my fragile body before I can answer. At 6 it is pure form RNG: Mega up means my Wallop beats his R suppress-slam; Mega down means he grabs me with his ult and I die. Never let him bait my Mega and then commit while I am reverting.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the danger zone and they belong to Sett. With Rage banked, a Mega Wallop stun or wall-combo wins the all-in outright — but caught in Mini when Facebreaker lands, his Haymaker and Pit Grit punches shred you before you can answer. At 6 it is form-dependent: Mega up, your Wallop beats The Show Stopper; Mega down, he grabs you and you die to a 120-second ultimate. Never let him bait the Mega, then commit while you revert — and buy anti-heal early, his missing-health regen fights your poke.

edits.after: True damage only in the center — stand at its edge and armour still holds.
